newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P says EMU-no will not hit Sweden's rating - paper.
newsitem.headline: S&P says EMU-no will not hit Sweden's rating - paper.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Tuesday that Sweden's rating would not be adversely affected if the government said "No" to joining Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.

The head of S&P's European ratings, Konrad Reuss, told daily newspaper Svenska Dagbladet that the state's strong financial development could be enough to raise Sweden's credit rating from AA+ in coming years.
"If we see a further significant improvement of state finances it could be an argument for a positive trend in the rating," Reuss told the paper.
"In the scenario we currently have for Sweden we don't see any risks for a negative trend."
But S&P, which changed its outlook for Sweden to stable from negative in April with a AA+ rating, expects to see modest wage increases and increased labour market flexibility, the daily said.
Reuss said S&P analysts were not bothered by expectations that the government will, on Tuesday, say no to joining EMU from the start in January 1999, the newspaper said.
"We have a more longterm view," Reuss said.
"We still expect that the Swedish government in the future, both before and after the (September) 1998 elections, will stick to the goals laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
"If the government deviated from this line, then we would certainly be concerned."
Reuss said Sweden would not necessarily need to tighten up its monetary and fiscal policies further if it stayed outside EMU.
